Priya (perf): Quick heads up — nightly perf run flagged a regression after the FP8 rollout when continuous batching is enabled. p95 latency up ~7% on short-seq workloads.
Liam: repro'd locally on A100-80GB, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN versions same as CI. Not a network fluke.
Ava: any chance KV cache layout changed? short sequences + cache hits could change kernel shapes.
Priya (perf): Good call. I profiled a small chat workload (seq<=32) with and without continuous batching. Key snippets: 
```
Baseline (FP32, no continuous batch): p95=45ms, mean tok/s=540
FP8 kernel, no continuous batch: p95=40ms, mean tok/s=620
FP8 kernel + continuous batch: p95=48ms, mean tok/s=470
```
We're seeing the FP8 kernel win for longer sequences, but drop below FP32 when continuous batching packs a lot of short requests together due to padding + kernel shape mismatch.
Diego: padding waste would normally help throughput though — why worse?
Priya (perf): The profiler shows two effects: 1) Kernel selection falls back to a generic matmul for many tiny batch x small-seq shapes (we lose the FP8 specialized kernel due to tile mismatch). 2) KV cache serialization currently re-chunks cached KV by request length, which creates many tiny GEMMs instead of a few medium ones. Combined overhead of kernel launch + extra memory moves dominates.
perf-bot: regression-alert: nightly-2026-02-12 FP8-cont-batching increased p95 on chat-smoke by 7.1% (tracked as RT-823).
Liam: Captured nvprof traces — attaching top lines: 
```
# hot kernels
fp8_matmul_tileA_32x128  cumulative 38%  avg 0.42ms
generic_gemm_1x64        cumulative 29%  avg 0.67ms (many launches)
kv_serialize_async       cumulative 10%  avg 0.18ms
```
The generic_gemm line correlates with many tiny launches.
Ava: So two approaches: better kernel routing (choose FP32/FP8 specialized vs generic by histogram) OR change batching to avoid creating those tiny shapes.
Priya (perf): I prototyped a kernel-selector heuristic that looks at per-worker seq_len histogram for last 60s and picks per-batch kernel by expected median sequence length. Quick numbers: 
```
old selector: always prefer fp8_specialized if model supports fp8
new selector (histogram): choose fp8_specialized only if median_seq >= 48
```
With that change, p95 for FP8+cont-batch on short-seq workload drops back to 43ms, mean tok/s=580.
Diego: Nice. Any downsides? Might hurt long-seq tails if we mis-route.
Priya (perf): Risk exists. We added a lightweight fallback: if runtime detects >15% more kernel launches than expected for a batch, immediately reroute next batch to alternative kernel. That gives graceful fallback without expensive rollouts.
Liam: Another angle — KV cache packing. Can we pack KV across requests when they share the same keyed block to reduce number of small GEMMs?
Ava: We already coalesce contiguous cache chunks per shard, but the current serializer emits per-request ops when continuous-batcher groups heterogeneous lengths. I sketched a change to emit per-shard aggregated ops with an index map.
Priya (perf): Implemented a prototype that 1) groups KV ops by shard/tile, 2) issues one batched GEMM with an indices gather at output. Result: kernel launches down ~35%, memory copies down ~20%. On short-seq FP8+cont-batch p95=41ms.
Diego: Any accuracy implications from aggregation/FP8 quantization? Calibration still same?
Priya (perf): No change to calibration path. We keep per-request scale factors; aggregation only changes how we schedule compute. Verified outputs against baseline with a small eval set — max token-level diff within expected FP8 quantization variance.
perf-bot: note: flagged candidate mitigations: histogram-based kernel-selector (PR draft), KV-agg-serializer (PR draft).
Liam: Can you post the selector pseudo-config you used? want to stress-test in DDP env.
Priya (perf): sure — config snippet: 
```
kernel_selector:
  strategy: "histogram_threshold"
  window_secs: 60
  median_threshold: 48
  launch_anomaly_threshold: 0.15
kv_serializer:
  strategy: "shard_aggregate"
  emit_index_map: true
```
Will push PRs for both tomorrow.
Ava: test matrix request: A100-80GB + T4 + p95/p99, workloads: chat-short (seq<=32), chat-mixed, long-context (seq>=1024), with/without continuous batching, with FP8/INT8/FP32.
Diego: I'll add the kernel-launch counters to the runtime metrics and surface them in the console per-route. That should make regressions obvious.
Priya (perf): Thanks — plan: land selector as canary, KV agg as follow-up. We'll keep FP8 rollout paused for cont-batching tier until canary shows no regression in 48h.
Liam: ack. Happy to pair on the DDP tests.
Ava: :thumbsup:
Priya (perf): Linking RT-823 for tracking and adding notes to the PRs.
Diego: small note — also validate with cuBLASLt backend, saw slightly different tile choices there.
Priya (perf): Good catch, include cuBLASLt/oneDNN permutations in stress matrix.
perf-bot: closing loop: RT-823 assigned to Priya, reviewer Diego."
